headline.note: Both figures are our own estimates, not measurements. The simulation is the rules engine behind Master League (matches, condition, money, calendar, contracts, transfers). It now runs 20 seasons on its own; what keeps it below 100 is the computer clubs' real transfer search, scouting, the user's transfer rules, a few international tournaments and some approximate parts. The whole mode also needs menus, transfer negotiation, news and saving, which are not started.

areas.name: Match results for computer teams
areas.text: Computer-versus-computer matches reproduce the real game's results and dice rolls, including cup extra time and penalties.

areas.name: Daily player condition
areas.text: Stamina, form, injury countdowns and the daily chance of a tiring injury follow the real game day by day. Morale after matches is mostly right but not fully.

areas.name: Competition calendar
areas.text: Leagues, domestic cups, promotion playoffs (including Chile's), Champions League, Europa League, Libertadores, AFC Champions League, Club World Cup, the World Cup and its qualifiers are built and scheduled as the game does. Draws for the next season's continental lists are exact. The game's calendar has no 29 February, and neither does the model.

areas.name: Finances
areas.text: Monthly income, prize money, match bonuses, gate receipts, the owner's reward and the fan count are modelled. Several of these match the game to the cent on the checked months.

areas.name: Player events
areas.text: The daily roll that decides which players get a special event is exact, provided the model is told the state the game tracks. Rebuilding that state from scratch is still being checked.

areas.name: Contracts, development and the season switch
areas.text: Loan returns, contract renewals, youth intake, the season-switch development and the replacement of retired players by new young players follow the game. Players also develop a second time on 1 January; the model matches the game's observed results there. Which players choose to retire is our own approximation.

areas.name: Computer-club transfers
areas.text: A behaviour model reproduces what computer clubs do in the summer and January windows: the numbers of transfers, loans and free signings and the squad shapes match the game's first two seasons. A moved player's new wage follows the game's rule. It is not the game's own search. The game's computer clubs pay no transfer fees and have no budgets, so by default the model has none either.

checks.intro: We saved snapshots of the real game on a Windows virtual machine, logged every random dice roll it made between them, and replayed the same days in our own engine. A result only counts when the model lands on the same numbers.

timeline.title: Project set up
timeline.text: Tools, notes and a first naming database exist; the host program starts on a Mac.

timeline.title: Game data readers and first competition rules
timeline.text: Archive and texture readers match reference tools; the first league and cup rules are read from the game.

timeline.title: League schedules and cups replay
timeline.text: Fixture lists and every knockout cup built at career start match the game.

timeline.title: Season set-up draws
timeline.text: The shuffles and draws used when a career season is built replay exactly.

timeline.title: Computer match simulation
timeline.text: The engine plays computer matches the way the game does, roll for roll, and updates daily condition.

timeline.title: A whole day, and the first season switch
timeline.text: Day-by-day driver, injuries, stamina and the first look at transfers and the season rollover.

timeline.title: Calendar, finances and contracts
timeline.text: Continental competitions, playoffs, a full free-running season, the first finance layers and contract expiry.

timeline.title: Player events and consistency
timeline.text: The daily player-event roll, Italy's playoff and the year-turn behaviour are added; replays are re-checked end to end.

timeline.title: World Cup draw and pending events
timeline.text: The World Cup draw is exact on two captures, and the list of pending player events is kept by the model.

timeline.title: Season-switch money, renewals and youth
timeline.text: Finances at the season switch, computer contract renewals and the youth intake follow the game.

timeline.title: Player-event tracking
timeline.text: The state behind the player-event roll is read from the game.

timeline.title: Accuracy plan and first audit
timeline.text: Exact where the rules are read, faithful behaviour elsewhere, approximations labelled. A first audit of five free-running seasons lists what is missing.

timeline.title: Computer transfers and long runs
timeline.text: Computer clubs now transfer, loan and sign free agents through both windows. Four 20-season runs found a leap-year bug, now fixed, and the World Cup qualifiers were added.

timeline.title: Player ratings and money
timeline.text: The second yearly development step stops ratings drifting down. Computer clubs turn out to have no money in the game, so the model's fees are switched off by default.
